identification.summary: China-origin threat actor that Microsoft tracks as Purple Typhoon (formerly POTASSIUM), mapped by Microsoft to APT10, MenuPass, Stone Panda and Red Apollo among other names [S1]. US prosecutors allege that two Chinese nationals linked to APT10 conducted global intrusion campaigns from at least 2006 through 2018 against managed service providers (MSPs), more than 45 technology companies in at least a dozen US states, and US government agencies [S2].
identification.firstObserved: At least 2006, per the December 2018 US indictment [S2].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Purple Typhoon (formerly POTASSIUM). Microsoft's mapping lists STONE PANDA, GOLEM, Evilgrab, AEON, LIVESAFE, ChChes, APT10, Haymaker, Webmonder, Foxtrot, Foxmail, MenuPass and Red Apollo as other names [S1]. 'CVNX' appears in DOJ material as a personal alias of the charged individual Zhu Hua, not as a vendor group name [S2]. MITRE tracks the group as menuPass (G0045). Cicada, BRONZE RIVERSIDE, Granite Taurus, TA429, HOGFISH and ATK41 are in this record's imported aliases but were not confirmed against a cited source in this research pass.

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China; the US Department of Justice alleges the charged APT10 members acted in association with the Ministry of State Security's (MSS) Tianjin State Security Bureau while working for Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company in Tianjin [S2].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft lists the actor's origin as China [S1]. The US government brought criminal charges (unproven allegations) against Zhu Hua and Zhang Shilong in December 2018 [S2]. No vendor confidence statement was gathered in this pass.
attribution.basis: DOJ indictment returned 2018-12-17 in the Southern District of New York and announced 2018-12-20, with FBI wanted notices [S2]; Microsoft naming taxonomy [S1].

objectives: Theft of intellectual property and confidential business information from technology companies, MSP clients and US government agencies, per the 2018 US indictment [S2].

sectors: Managed service providers and their clients [S2]
regions: United States (technology companies in at least a dozen states) [S2]
targeting.notes: Sector and regional detail is limited to what the indictment summary states [S2]. Country-level victim lists for the MSP campaign were not verified in this pass.

capabilities.summary: Compromise of managed service providers to reach their clients' networks, enabling large-scale theft of intellectual property and business data [S2]. Malware and tooling detail was not gathered from cited sources in this pass; see the MITRE G0045 software list.

campaigns.name: Technology and government intrusion campaign
campaigns.summary: DOJ alleges intrusions into more than 45 technology companies in at least a dozen US states and into US government agencies.

campaigns.name: Managed service provider campaign (commonly called Cloud Hopper)
campaigns.summary: DOJ alleges APT10 members compromised MSPs to steal intellectual property and confidential business information from their clients; the 'Cloud Hopper' label is industry usage not taken from the cited source.

campaigns.name: US indictment of Zhu Hua and Zhang Shilong
campaigns.summary: Grand jury in SDNY returned charges of conspiracy to commit computer intrusion, wire fraud conspiracy and aggravated identity theft on 2018-12-17; unsealed and announced 2018-12-20.

diamond.adversary: PRC operators; charged individuals Zhu Hua and Zhang Shilong of Huaying Haitai, associated with the MSS Tianjin State Security Bureau [S2].
diamond.capability: MSP compromise as an access path to client networks; data theft [S2].
diamond.victim: MSPs and their clients, more than 45 US technology companies and US government agencies [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection of intellectual property and business information to benefit PRC interests, as alleged by DOJ [S2].
diamond.technology: Trusted administrative access held by MSPs into client environments [S2].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain includes the MSPs, IT outsourcers and contractor networks that hold administrative access into DoD-adjacent and defense-industrial environments [S2]. STEP 2: Trusted third-party access lets the actor bypass perimeter defenses of the ultimate target [S2]. STEP 3: The template is compromise of a service provider, pivot through its trusted connections into client networks, then theft of intellectual property and business data [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is sustained IP theft from technology and government clients through shared service providers. MDCOA is simultaneous access to many defense-sector clients through one compromised provider, used for collection or pre-positioning during a crisis. Candidate indicators: anomalous logins from MSP administrative accounts outside contracted windows, and unexpected bulk data movement from client environments to provider-managed hosts.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness should map which mission systems depend on third-party administrators [S2]. (2) Authorities: activity crossing from contractor or MSP networks into DoD systems will need coordination with law enforcement (FBI), consistent with the DOJ-led 2018 action [S2]. (3) Mission assurance: restrict and monitor provider access paths. (4) Coordinate with DC3 and the DIB CS program on provider-sourced intrusions.
